claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of CD8+ T cells from lymph nodes, bone marrow, spleen, lung showed that lymph-node memory CD8+ T cells have a distinct protein-expression profile characterized by TCF-1 and CD28 enrichment, separating them from more effector-like T-bet and Granzyme B–associated CD8+ T-cell populations at other tissue sites.

sources.quote: We used cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) to define a protein expression signature of LN memory CD8 + T cells relative to other sites based on the transcriptional profile identified above.

The concatenated analysis reveals that TCF-1 and CD28 segregate on distinct regions of the t-SNE plots relative to T-bet and Granzyme B expression (Fig. 4A), which correspond to naïve (CD45RA+CCR7+) and TEMRA cells (CD45RA+CCR7-), respectively (Fig. 4B).

comparison.finding: LN memory CD8+ T cells exhibit a distinct protein expression signature compared to bone marrow
LN memory CD8+ T cells exhibit a distinct protein expression signature compared to spleen
LN memory CD8+ T cells exhibit a distinct protein expression signature compared to lungs

claim_2.claim: T cell receptor repertoire sequencing of CD8+ TEM cells from lymph nodes and bone marrow from five individuals showed that lymph-node memory CD8+ T cells maintained higher TCR diversity and lower clonality than bone-marrow memory CD8+ T cells.

sources.quote: We found an increased number of different V region sequences from comparable numbers of LN compared to BM memory CD8 + T cells for all donors.

comparison.finding: LN memory CD8+ T cells maintain higher TCR diversity compared to BM memory CD8+ T cells

claim_3.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of anti-CD3/anti-CD28-stimulated memory CD8+ T cells showed that lymph-node memory CD8+ T cells had greater proliferative capacity than memory CD8+ T cells from bone marrow, spleen, and lung, with lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells showing markedly higher post-stimulation cell counts and greater T-bet induction compared with other tissue sites.

sources.quote: When stimulated with anti-CD3/anti-CD28 antibodies, LN memory CD8+T cells exhibited greater proliferation compared to counterparts in BM, spleen and lung (Fig. 6A, C).
After CD3/CD28 stimulation, LN CD8+TEM cell counts were between 98–106 fold higher than BM.

T-bet expression, was also increased to a greater extent in LN CD8+TEM cells following stimulation compared to other sites both in the level of expression and the fold-change increase following activation (Fig. 6B, D).
Together, these results demonstrate that LN memory CD8+T cells have a higher capacity for proliferation and differentiation compared to memory CD8+T cells in other sites.

comparison.finding: lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells also showed greater T-bet induction after stimulation
lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells also showed greater T-bet induction after stimulation
lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells also showed greater T-bet induction after stimulation

claim_4.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of CD8+ TEM cells showed that lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells had significantly higher TCF-1 expression than CD8+ TEM cells from blood, bone marrow, spleen, and lung, with TCF-1hi CD8+ TEM cells observed across lymph nodes draining different anatomical sites and across donors aged 9–76 years.

sources.quote: We examined whether CD8+TEM cells exhibited tissue-specific variations in expression of TCF-1, a transcription factor associated with stem-like function.(9)
In all donors, TCF-1 expression by CD8+TEM in LN was significantly higher than that found in CD8+TEM derived from blood, BM, spleen, and lung (Fig. 1B).
TCF-1hiCD8+TEM cells were observed in LN draining different anatomical sites (lungs, intestines, groin, Fig. 1B) and across all ages (9–76 years, Fig. 1C).

comparison.finding: lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells showed significantly higher TCF-1 expression than blood CD8+ TEM cells
lymph-node CD8+ TEM cells showed significantly higher TCF-1 expression than bone-marrow CD8+ TEM cells
